<b>Грудино-ключично-сосцевидная мышца</b: The sternocleidomastoid runs from the manubrium and clavicle to the mastoid process behind the ear and divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles. One muscle turns the face to the opposite side and tilts the head toward its own shoulder; both together flex the neck. Nerve: accessory.
<b>Трапециевидная мышца</b> (верхняя час: The trapezius (upper part) runs from the occipital bone and nuchal ligament to the outer third of the clavicle, the acromion and the scapular spine. It shrugs the shoulders and tips the head back. Its front edge is the back border of the posterior triangle. Nerve: accessory.
<b>Надподъязычные мышцы</b> — двубрюшная: The suprahyoid muscles: the digastric (anterior belly from the chin, posterior belly from the mastoid process, tendon near the hyoid) and the mylohyoid, the floor of the mouth. They raise the hyoid and larynx during swallowing and help open the mouth.
<b>Лестничные мышцы</b> — передняя, сред: The scalenes (anterior, middle and posterior) run from the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae to the 1st and 2nd ribs. They lift the ribs in deep breathing and bend the neck. The brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle; the subclavian vein, in front of the anterior.
<b>Ременная мышца головы</b> и <b>мышца,: The splenius capitis and levator scapulae, with the scalenes, form the floor of the posterior triangle. The splenius runs from the spinous processes to the mastoid process: it extends and turns the head. The levator runs from the transverse processes of C1–C4 to the upper angle of the scapula.
<b>Подкожная мышца шеи</b> (платизма) —: The platysma is a thin sheet just under the skin, from the chest below the clavicle to the mandible and the corner of the mouth. It tenses the skin of the neck and pulls the corners of the mouth down. It is a muscle of facial expression, supplied by the facial nerve. Shown see-through here.
<b>Подподбородочный треугольник</b> — не: The submental triangle is unpaired: between the anterior bellies of the two digastrics and the body of the hyoid; its floor is the mylohyoid. It holds the submental lymph nodes, which receive lymph from the tip of the tongue, the floor of the mouth and the lower lip.
<b>Поднижнечелюстной треугольник</b> — м: The submandibular triangle lies between the lower edge of the mandible and the two bellies of the digastric. It holds the submandibular salivary gland and lymph nodes; the facial artery, facial vein and hypoglossal nerve pass through it.
<b>Сонный треугольник</b> — между грудин: The carotid triangle is bounded by the sternocleidomastoid, the posterior belly of the digastric and the superior belly of the omohyoid. Here the common carotid artery divides, and the internal jugular vein, vagus and hypoglossal nerves pass. This is where the pulse is felt.
<b>Лопаточно-трахеальный (мышечный) треу: The muscular (omotracheal) triangle lies between the midline, the sternocleidomastoid and the superior belly of the omohyoid. Under the strap muscles lie the larynx, trachea and thyroid gland, so this is the surgical route to them.
<b>Лопаточно-трапециевидный треугольник<: The occipital (omotrapezoid) triangle is the upper, larger part of the posterior triangle: between the sternocleidomastoid, the trapezius and the inferior belly of the omohyoid. The accessory nerve crosses it obliquely and is easily injured during lymph node biopsy.
<b>Лопаточно-ключичный треугольник</b> —: The supraclavicular (omoclavicular) triangle lies above the middle third of the clavicle, below the inferior belly of the omohyoid. It holds the subclavian artery and the trunks of the brachial plexus: the site for numbing the arm and for pressing the artery against the 1st rib.
<b>Общая сонная артерия</b> поднимается: The common carotid artery rises in the carotid sheath and divides at the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage (C4) into the internal carotid, to the brain and eye, with no branches in the neck, and the external carotid, which feeds the thyroid, tongue, face and scalp. The carotid sinus, a pressure sensor, sits at the start of the internal.
<b>Подключичная артерия</b> перекидывает: The subclavian artery arches over the 1st rib behind the anterior scalene and heads to the arm. It gives off the vertebral artery, which climbs through the transverse foramina of C6–C1 into the skull to the brainstem and cerebellum, and the inferior thyroid artery.
<b>Внутренняя яремная вена</b> несёт кро: The internal jugular vein drains the brain, face and neck. It lies in the carotid sheath lateral to the artery and joins the subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint (the venous angle). The external jugular runs over the sternocleidomastoid and bulges when you strain.
<b>Блуждающий нерв</b> (X пара) спускает: The vagus nerve (CN X) descends in the carotid sheath, behind and between the artery and vein, to the heart, lungs and gut. The right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under the subclavian artery, the left under the aortic arch; both climb to the larynx between the trachea and esophagus.
<b>Диафрагмальный нерв</b> (C3–C5) спуск: The phrenic nerve (C3–C5) runs down the anterior scalene into the chest to the diaphragm, so a neck injury above C3 stops breathing. The brachial plexus (C5–T1) emerges between the anterior and middle scalenes and passes above the clavicle to the arm as three trunks.
<b>Добавочный нерв</b> (XI пара) выходит: The accessory nerve (CN XI) leaves the skull through the jugular foramen, supplies the sternocleidomastoid, then crosses the posterior triangle obliquely and passes under the trapezius. It lies superficially; if it is injured, the shoulder droops and the arm is hard to raise above shoulder height.
<b>Кожные ветви шейного сплетения</b> (C: The skin branches of the cervical plexus (C2–C4) emerge from behind the back edge of the sternocleidomastoid at almost one spot, the nerve point, near its middle: great auricular, lesser occipital, transverse cervical and supraclavicular nerves. Anesthetic is injected here.
<b>Предтрахеальная пластинка</b> — мышеч: The pretracheal layer has a muscular sheet around the strap muscles and a visceral one: the capsule of the thyroid and the sleeve of the trachea and esophagus (behind, the buccopharyngeal fascia). The gland is tied to the larynx, so its nodules rise when you swallow.
<b>Сонное влагалище</b> — фасциальная тр: The carotid sheath is a fascial tube on each side of the neck organs. Inside: the common carotid artery (medial), internal jugular vein (lateral) and vagus nerve (behind, between them). The ansa cervicalis runs down its front; the sympathetic trunk lies behind it.
<b>Предпозвоночная пластинка</b> охватыв: The prevertebral layer wraps the spine and its muscles: longus colli, scalenes and the deep back muscles. Under it lie the phrenic nerve and the roots of the brachial plexus; the sympathetic trunk lies on it. The plexus and subclavian artery carry it to the arm as a sheath.
<b>Заглоточное пространство</b> — щель м: The retropharyngeal space is the gap between the pharynx and esophagus in front and the prevertebral layer behind. The alar fascia splits it in two; the back part, the danger space, runs from the skull base to the diaphragm, so pus from a retropharyngeal abscess can drain into the mediastinum.
<b>Шея</b> соединяет голову с туловищем:: The neck links head and trunk: it carries the airway, the esophagus, the vessels of the brain and the nerves to the arms and diaphragm. Its frame is seven cervical vertebrae, the hyoid and the larynx. The muscles lie in layers: platysma, sternocleidomastoid and trapezius, strap muscles in front, scalenes deep.
<b>Треугольники шеи</b> — карта для врач: The triangles of the neck are a map for doctors. The sternocleidomastoid splits each side into an anterior triangle (midline, mandible, muscle) and a posterior one (muscle, trapezius, clavicle). The digastric and omohyoid divide them into smaller ones, each with its own contents.
<b>Сосуды и нервы шеи.</b> Главный пучок: Vessels and nerves of the neck. The main bundle is the common carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve in one fascial tube, the carotid sheath, under the sternocleidomastoid (see-through here). Deeper, on the scalenes, lie the phrenic nerve and the brachial plexus.
<b>Разрез шеи на уровне VII шейного позв: Section of the neck at the level of C7, seen from above, front at the top. Fasciae divide the neck into compartments: the investing layer surrounds everything, the pretracheal layer the organs, the prevertebral layer the spine and its muscles, the carotid sheaths the neurovascular bundles. Pus and blood spread along the gaps between them.
верхний край щитовидного хряща: upper edge of the thyroid cartilage
Узкий мост между головой и туловищем: че: A narrow bridge between head and trunk that carries air, food and blood to the brain, and nerves to the arms. Its muscles divide it into triangles that doctors use to find the pulse, lymph nodes and vessels.
<b>Подподъязычные мышцы</b> — плоские ле: The infrahyoid (strap) muscles are flat bands in front: sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and omohyoid (two bellies joined by a tendon under the sternocleidomastoid). They pull the hyoid and larynx back down after swallowing. Nerve supply: ansa cervicalis (C1–C3).
<b>Подъязычный нерв</b> (XII пара) — дви: The hypoglossal nerve (CN XII), the motor nerve of the tongue, loops around the outside of the internal and external carotids above the bifurcation and runs forward above the hyoid. C1 fibers travel with it and leave as the superior root of the ansa cervicalis to the strap muscles.
с каждой стороны и непарный: on each side, plus one unpaired
<b>Поверхностная пластинка</b> шейной фа: The investing layer of the deep cervical fascia surrounds the whole neck under the platysma and splits around the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius (near the mandible, around the submandibular and parotid glands). It attaches to the mandible and occiput above and to the clavicles and sternum below.
\n <div><h2>Строение</h2>\n:
Structure

The neck runs from the lower edge of the mandible and the skull base down to the clavicles, the manubrium and the 7th cervical vertebra, whose spinous process sticks out most and is easy to feel. Landmarks in front: the hyoid at C3, the thyroid cartilage at C4–C5, the cricoid at C6; below it the trachea and esophagus begin. The thyroid gland wraps the trachea below the cricoid, its isthmus lying on rings 2–4.

The muscles come in layers: the platysma (a muscle of facial expression, supplied by the facial nerve); the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius, both supplied by the accessory nerve and both enclosed in the investing fascia; the supra- and infrahyoid muscles, which raise and lower the hyoid with the larynx; and the deep scalene and prevertebral muscles.

Landmarks

The carotid pulse is felt at the front edge of the sternocleidomastoid at the level of the thyroid cartilage, pressing the artery against the transverse process of C6. The external jugular vein swells with straining, shouting and heart failure. Near the middle of the back edge of the sternocleidomastoid, the skin nerves of the cervical plexus emerge from under it: the nerve point.

Medicine

  • Tracheostomy is an opening below the cricoid through tracheal rings 2–4; the thyroid isthmus and veins lie in the way. In an emergency, cricothyrotomy through the cricothyroid ligament is faster.
  • Torticollis (wry neck) is a shortened sternocleidomastoid: the head tilts toward the affected side and the face turns to the other.
  • Narrowing of the internal carotid by an atherosclerotic plaque at the bifurcation is a common cause of stroke; it shows on ultrasound, and the plaque is removed or a stent is placed.
  • Deep neck infections (retropharyngeal abscess, floor-of-mouth cellulitis) spread along the fascial spaces, even into the mediastinum.
  • An enlarged lymph node in the neck is usually due to a throat or tooth infection; a hard, painless node that has not shrunk in 3–4 weeks should be seen by a doctor.
  • Thoracic outlet syndrome is compression of the brachial plexus and subclavian artery between the scalenes (for example, by an extra cervical rib): numbness and weakness of the arm.

Simplifications

  • In the 3D modes, muscles, vessels and nerves are built schematically after the atlas, without skin, fat, lymph nodes or salivary glands; the head and shoulder girdle are shown only in part. The stylohyoid and geniohyoid are not shown, and the two heads of the sternocleidomastoid are merged.
  • The two sides are symmetric, except for the origins of the vessels in the chest and the recurrent laryngeal nerves. The brachial plexus is reduced to five roots and three trunks; the sympathetic trunk appears only in the section.
  • The triangles are drawn on a simplified neck surface. The section is a diagram at the level of C7 with skin and subcutaneous tissue, seen from above (the person’s right side is on the right); CT scans and the atlas usually show sections from below, mirrored.
